why: 'You marched across the earth with fury' is said to God, whose 'flying arrows' and 'shining spear' the verse before describes.
'the daughter of Herodias danced before them and pleased Herod' makes her the one doing the pleasing; Herod is the one pleased.
'Heal me, O LORD, and I will be healed' asks the LORD to do the healing.

correct_doer: they (the Chaldeans, named in the verse before)
why: 'And they slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah ... Then they put out his eyes ... and took him to Babylon' gives the action to 'they', and Nebuchadnezzar is not in the verse.
'Will you stay on the ancient path' is a question put to the one addressed as 'you', Job, in Eliphaz's speech.
'look on every proud man and bring him low' is commanded of the 'your' addressed in the verse before, 'adorn yourself with majesty'.
'I have indeed built You an exalted house' is spoken by Solomon, named in the verse before ('Then Solomon declared').
'his sins, which he caused Israel to commit' makes Israel the one committing the sins; the verse says he caused it.
'So that is what the soldiers did' gives the dividing to the soldiers, and 'magistrates' appears nowhere in the verse.
'do not imitate what is evil, but what is good' is addressed to 'Beloved', whom 3 John 1:1 names as Gaius ('To the beloved Gaius').
'Should he have treated our sister like a prostitute?' is the brothers' accusation against 'he', who is Shechem, the one who 'took her and lay with her by force' (Gen 34:2).
'you people do not accept our testimony' is said to the 'Israel's teacher' addressed as 'you' in the verse before, of whom Nicodemus is the one named.
'you must surely redeem every firstborn son' is addressed to Aaron, to whom 'the LORD said' in Num 18:1.
'He brought us to this place and gave us this land' has the LORD as subject, the one who 'brought us out of Egypt' in the verse before.
'that our God will count you worthy of His calling' makes God the one who counts, which fills the unnamed doer slot.
'Moses saw that the people were out of control, for Aaron had let them run wild' makes the people the ones out of control; Aaron is the cause.
'Now I have brought it to pass' is God's speech, as the verse's 'Long ago I ordained it' shows.
'he took her as a wife and slept with her' has 'he' as Judah, the subject of 'Judah saw' in the same verse.
'all that the LORD had commanded him' has the LORD as the one who commands.
'what I command you' is spoken by Moses, the speaker of Deuteronomy ('the words that Moses spoke', Deut 1:1).
'He provides food for those who fear Him' has 'He', the LORD of the verse before ('the LORD is gracious and compassionate'), as subject.
'And they shouted back, Crucify Him!' gives the cry to the crowd, not to Pilate, who only asked 'What then do you want me to do'.
'Then the king said to Zadok, Return the ark of God to the city' commands Zadok, who is the one to return it.
'So they ran and brought Saul' gives the bringing to 'they', the people who had inquired of the LORD in the verse before; the kingdom is not the subject.
'But Elymas the sorcerer ... opposed them' is the same sorcerer named Bar-Jesus in Acts 13:6, so the record's name is the same man.
'The mighty King loves justice' makes the King the one who loves; 'strength' is not in the verse.
'for the LORD has rejected and forsaken the generation of His wrath' has the LORD as the one who forsakes.
'You hear its sound' is said to the one addressed in the verse before as 'You must be born again', Nicodemus.
'Then Jehoash brought him to Jerusalem and broke down the wall of Jerusalem' has Jehoash as subject.
'The whole world sought an audience with Solomon' makes the whole world the one seeking; the record's 'ground' is the same subject.
'This third I will bring through the fire; I will refine them like silver' has the LORD ('declares the LORD' in the verse before) as the one refining.
'This is why I am commanding you to set apart for yourselves three cities' is spoken by Moses, the speaker of Deuteronomy (Deut 1:1).
'I will make your oppressors eat their own flesh' has God causing it; the oppressors are the ones who eat.
'He said to Jacob, Let me eat some of that red stew, for I am famished' gives the eating-request to Esau; Jacob replies in the next verse.
'Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused Israel to sin' makes Israel the one who sins; Jeroboam is the one who caused it.
'They will bring a mob against you, who will stone you' has the mob, which the record calls company, as the one stoning.
'the rams of Nebaioth will serve you' makes the rams the ones who serve.
'these were the ones Joshua circumcised' gives the circumcising to Joshua; the sons of Israel are those circumcised, and the verse says they were uncircumcised.
'his sin, which he had caused Israel to commit' makes Israel the one committing; Jeroboam is the one who caused it.
'Ahab served Baal a little, but Jehu will serve him a lot' has Ahab as the one who served Baal.
